overall_quality.evidence: Hash tables use a variety of methods to handle collisions, including chaining and open addressing. Chaining involves storing collided items in a linked list at the same index. Open addressing, on the other hand, finds the next available slot in the table to store the item. Both methods are effective, but chaining is generally simpler to implement.
